What the next slice is
The menu plan's own closing register names it, in as many words: "Nothing measures §11.1 with a picture on a card … It is the cheapest remaining thing in this file." That is Stage 1e, and its recorded blocker is precise — attaching a photograph inside scenario 21 means extracting the upload journey into the harness.

I confirmed the blocker is real and the shape of the work:

The upload journey exists only inline inside MenuPictureScenarios, with #picture-file, #picture-status, .status-success and img.manage-picture-image as private const. A second scenario file cannot reach any of it — F-100's situation exactly, one register over from TableJourneys.SeatGuestAsync in Slice 64.
PictureFixtures.SquareGradientPng(edge) already generates a real PNG of a chosen size, so no fixture work is needed. At edge 400 the file is 480,503 bytes against §8.2's cap of 524,288 — inside it, so menu-picture.js reports "stored exactly as it is" and the server stores a 400×400 PNG verbatim. No JPEG re-encode, no ladder, nothing non-deterministic.
Why 400 and not 12. .order-menu-detail-picture carries max-width: 100%; height: auto, and that stylesheet's own comment says why: "a 3000px photograph would make the DOCUMENT wider than a 375px viewport". A 12px fixture renders 12px and proves the declaration does nothing. A 400px intrinsic image inside a ~300px panel is the arrangement in which that declaration is load-bearing — remove it and ScrollsSideways fails.

And the vacuity trap I found on the way in, which is F-41's shape. An <img> that has not decoded has zero intrinsic size, so its box is 0×0 — and a 0×0 box trivially lies inside the viewport. Worse, the required-selector census would report img.order-menu-detail-picture × 1, matched, so Slice 64's own refusal cannot see it. The barrier would pass while measuring a placeholder. The card's thumbnail is loading="eager" only for heading index 0, which is where scenario 21's items sit — true today, and not a contract.

That makes two things load-bearing rather than tidy: a decode wait in the harness before measuring, and a collapsed-box refusal in the barrier scoped to a new selector group for elements sized by their own bytes rather than by padding and text.
